subject: english-language
title: The PEEL Plan
welcome_lead: Build a paragraph that proves what you infer.
meta_desc: KS3 English Language adventure on the PEEL paragraph structure.
final_note: You can now write a clear PEEL paragraph from a short text.

concepts.def: Quote or detail supporting the point.
Why the evidence proves the point.

walkthroughs.body_html: Point, Evidence, Explain, Link. Use this order to build a strong inference paragraph.
Quotes work best embedded: 'When Tom "slammed" the door, his fury is clear.' Quote inside your own sentence.
In the Explain step, decode the writer's choice — verb, image, sound — and link it to character or theme.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between voiced and voiceless sounds?
options: Voiced sounds are produced with vocal-fold vibration (/b/, /d/, /g/, /z/); voiceless sounds without it (/p/, /t/, /k/, /s/). You can feel the difference by putting a hand on your throat.
Voiced sounds are loud and voiceless sounds are whispered.
Voiced sounds use the lips; voiceless sounds use the tongue.
Both terms mean the same — analysing language scientifically.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between semantics and pragmatics?
options: Both terms mean the same — analysing language scientifically.
Semantics studies literal meaning of words and sentences; pragmatics studies how meaning depends on context, speaker intention and conversational implicature.
Semantics is grammar and pragmatics is vocabulary.
Semantics is speech and pragmatics is writing.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between descriptive and prescriptive approaches to language?
options: Descriptivists describe how language is actually used; prescriptivists rule on how language ought to be used — modern linguistics is descriptivist.
Semantics is speech and pragmatics is writing.
Descriptivists describe written language and prescriptivists describe spoken language.
Both terms mean the same — analysing language scientifically.
